title: China to fly Pakistan's first astronaut to its space station on Shenzhou-24 on Wednesday
dek: Muhammad Zeeshan Ali will be the first foreign visitor to Tiangong, as China and Pakistan mark 75 years of ties and India's own crewed programme waits for its first uncrewed test.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
China will launch Pakistan's first astronaut to its Tiangong space station early on Wednesday, the first time a foreign national has flown on a Chinese crewed mission. The Shenzhou-24 spacecraft is due to lift off on a Long March-2F rocket from the Jiuquan launch centre in north-west China at 8.18 am Beijing time on 25 November (5.48 am IST), the China Manned Space Agency said when it named the crew on Tuesday.

Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, a Pakistan Air Force pilot, will fly as payload specialist alongside the mission commander, Tang Hongbo, a veteran of two earlier flights, and the pilot, Wu Yi, on his first. Mr Ali is expected to spend about a week on the station and return on the Shenzhou-23 spacecraft, while his two Chinese crewmates stay for a six-month rotation. The crew plans about 90 experiments, the agency's spokesperson Zhang Jingbo said, according to reports.

## Beijing and Islamabad

Asked about the mission at Tuesday's briefing, China's foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun called it a milestone for the country's space programme and for relations with Pakistan, which mark their 75th anniversary this year. "The Pakistani astronaut will be the first visiting foreign astronaut to China's space station," he said. "We wish the mission a full success."

Pakistan's space agency Suparco and the Chinese agency signed the agreement for the flight in February 2025; it provided for two Pakistanis to train in China and one to fly. Mr Ali and Khurram Daud were selected in April this year. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif called the flight a historic moment and thanked President Xi Jinping, and Mr Ali described the mission as "a launch pad" for future joint flights, including to the Moon, according to reports.

China has been excluded from the International Space Station since 2011, when a US law barred NASA from working with Chinese agencies, and has since built its own station and sought foreign partners. It aims to land astronauts on the Moon by 2030. China has also launched Pakistani satellites, including the PRSS-1 remote-sensing satellite in 2018.

## What it means for India

The flight adds a crewed-spaceflight strand to a China-Pakistan partnership that already spans defence, the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor and satellites, several of which have military as well as civilian uses. For India, it is a further sign of Beijing extending its strategic technology to Islamabad, a partnership Indian officials have long watched closely.

It also lands as India's own human spaceflight programme, Gaganyaan, prepares for its first uncrewed orbital test. ISRO chairman V Narayanan said this month that the G1 mission, carrying the humanoid robot Vyommitra, was scheduled for December, according to reports; other reports since then say it is unlikely before February 2027, which ISRO has not confirmed. India's only astronauts so far have flown with foreign partners: Rakesh Sharma on a Soviet mission in 1984 and Shubhanshu Shukla on the commercial Axiom-4 flight to the International Space Station in 2025. India plans its own station, the Bharatiya Antariksh Station, by 2035.

## What happens next

If the launch goes to schedule, Shenzhou-24 is expected to dock with Tiangong within hours. The current crew, including Hong Kong's first astronaut, Lai Ka-ying, will return to Earth with Mr Ali after the handover, while Zhu Yangzhu stays on board for what is planned as China's first year-long stay in space.
